saying: Most commenters say prespecifying each future change is unworkable for generative systems and ask FDA to authorize a bounded change envelope instead: locked benchmarks, acceptance thresholds and non-inferiority margins, verification, monitoring, rollback, and triggers for a new submission. Several add tiered change categories and specific handling of third-party foundation model updates, including contracts, version control, and triggered revalidation.

disagreement.text: No material conflict appeared: commenters converge on boundary- or invariant-based PCCPs and instead debate implementation details  enchmark suites must be locked and escrowed, how change tiers are defined, and what falls inside the envelope, including model compression, third-party model updates, and changes in the clinical environment.
